original_value: In the last decade, the usage of Augmented Reality (AR) has proliferated especially in the education sector. However, only limited articles have systematically reviewed the research trends in the implementation of AR for learning mathematics. Thus, this paper presents a systematic and comprehensive analysis of the research trend for the period between the year 2015–2019. From a leading indexing Scopus database, this review has identified only 19 journal articles based on the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework. These works of literature were analyzed and grouped into eight themes to illustrate the trends of these research focus: AR apps types, AR apps development tools, research contribution cat-egories, benefits of AR for math, learning problems, testing methods, and math subtopics. Moreover, this synthesized review on learning of mathematics through AR could benefit researchers and educators, thereby suggesting avenues for future research.

result.paraphrase: Over the past decade, Augmented Reality (AR) has spread rapidly, particularly in education. Yet only a few studies have systematically examined research trends in using AR to teach mathematics. This paper therefore provides a systematic, comprehensive analysis of research trends from 2015 to 2019. Using the Scopus indexing database and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework, the review identified just 19 journal articles. These studies were organized into eight themes to show the direction of the research: AR app types, AR app development tools, categories of research contributions, benefits of AR for mathematics, learning issues, testing methods, and mathematics subtopics. In addition, this synthesized review of mathematics learning through AR may help researchers and educators and point to future research directions.
